title: Replace valueType with orthogonal fieldType facets
decision_statement: A Field expresses datatype, cardinality, value domain, format, and constraints as independent fieldType facets instead of extending the conflated valueType enum with more parallel patch properties.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-032 Change A replaces valueType with the decomposed fieldType model; its rationale records the rejected ninth-value alternative.
The effective Field schema requires fieldType and defines its orthogonal facets.

alternatives: Keep valueType and add composite as a ninth enum value.
Keep separate contentFormat, allowed-values, validation-rule, and repeatable mechanisms.
accepted_cost: All Field definitions required a breaking, scripted definition-layer migration and existing readers temporarily could not load them.
supersedes: Field.valueType and its parallel patch-property model

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Keeping convenient legacy encodings would preserve ambiguity between independent semantic facets.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Presentation concerns remain available outside fieldType.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: The semantic model becomes harder to author than the ambiguity it removes.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserving the public legacy shape would freeze a model unable to describe itself.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The migration was deterministic, idempotent, corpus-wide, and instance cutover was separately gated.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Breaking changes land without complete migration and compatibility evidence.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Parallel mechanisms would permit incompatible descriptions of the same concern.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Package-managed vocabularies and open maps preserve bounded extension points.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: One core type vocabulary crowds out legitimate domain-owned meaning.

coding_notes: Atomic choice is replacement of the type-description mechanism; individual new datatype constructs are separate cards. Matches calibrated precedent E256-A90 without reusing its research ID.

title: Model composite range as a typed reference with explicit storage mode
decision_statement: Composite Field ranges use an exact Type reference and declare inline versus reference storage explicitly; recursive inline range graphs are rejected while reference edges terminate recursion.

sources.excerpt: Accepted Change B makes rangeType an ExactTypeRef, requires an explicit inline/reference mode, and defines the two storage forms.
The delivered conformance fixture covers inline and reference modes and their projections.

alternatives: Use untyped nested JSON objects.
Infer storage mode from the value shape.
Permit recursive inline object graphs without a reference break.
accepted_cost: Authors must name and version the range Type, choose storage mode, and respect a well-founded recursion rule.
supersedes: FieldGroup as the only inline-composite range mechanism
derived_from: RFC-032 owner decisions D2 and D4

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Anonymous or inferred objects would lose stable range identity and make storage semantics ambiguous.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Inline mode keeps ordinary nested data directly expressible; reference mode remains a UUID string.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Every nested shape is forced into a separately managed Type without practical benefit.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Retaining scalar-only ranges would prevent self-hosting and nested model evolution.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Exact version references and a recursion base case preserve resolvability.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Range evolution strands values or changes referenced identities.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Each consumer could infer a different nested shape or reference convention.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Packages own the referenced Types and choose inline or reference mode per Field.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Shared range rules eliminate useful package-local object forms.

coding_notes: The exact range and explicit storage mode form the one ref datatype contract; FieldGroup migration timing is separate.

title: Prefer typed specializations over a general union or JSON escape hatch
decision_statement: The field model adds only the demonstrated dependent and bounded-map shapes and resolves apparent unions through dependent typing, cardinality, or discriminated families; it does not add a general sum type or free-JSON datatype.

sources.excerpt: RFC-032 says no irreducible sum was found, accepts a bounded map for recurring extension bags, and rejects a free JSON/object value type as untyped and unprojectable.
The paper proof exercises dependent, map, and discriminated-family cases without a sum construct.

alternatives: Add a general oneOf/sum range.
Add a free JSON or object datatype.
Omit open maps even where extension bags recur.
accepted_cost: Some heterogeneous constraints require named discriminators or semantic validation rather than a concise union, and maps must declare a bounded value range.
derived_from: RFC-032 owner decisions D5 and D6

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A general escape hatch would be easier to author but would conceal meaning and defeat projection.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: A bounded map is included because open extension bags are a demonstrated practical need.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Avoiding a general construct creates numerous bespoke types for genuinely heterogeneous values.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: The sources do not compare historical compatibility costs for this construct choice.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: A future proven union need is rejected merely because none existed in this corpus.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Free JSON would let every package invent an opaque sub-language.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Open map keys remain package-defined and valueRange may be declared or open.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: The shared core absorbs domain-specific shapes that belong in package Types.

coding_notes: One architectural boundary: add only evidenced typed expressive power, reject general opaque polymorphism.

title: Keep presentation hints outside the semantic type model
decision_statement: Editor and composite-renderer hints remain presentation-layer concerns and are not encoded as fieldType facets.

sources.excerpt: The accepted rationale says editorHint and compositeRenderer map to no semantic axis and are consolidated by the rendering follow-up instead of fieldType.
The effective schema retains editorHint separately from fieldType.

alternatives: Treat input widgets and composite renderers as semantic type facets.
accepted_cost: Presentation behavior needs a separate view-layer contract and cannot be recovered from Field meaning alone.
derived_from: RFC-032 owner decision D3 scope clarification

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Putting display or input modality into fieldType would make a practical rendering choice appear semantic.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The hints are retained and assigned to a dedicated rendering follow-up rather than deleted.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Separation prevents a renderer from obtaining semantic role information it genuinely requires.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: No temporal tradeoff decides this boundary.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: A later migration changes hint ownership without preserving existing presentations.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Type-owned presentation would impose one modality on every view and consumer.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The later rendering contract supplies shared dispatch and fallback rules.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: View-local choices become mutually unintelligible or non-portable.

coding_notes: This card records the layer boundary only; RFC-036 rendering ownership belongs to family B.

title: Subsume FieldGroup semantically but gate its data removal on a carrier
decision_statement: The typed inline-ref mechanism becomes the semantic replacement for FieldGroup, while deprecated FieldGroup and assignment carrier members remain until #242 can migrate inline-composite instance values atomically.

sources.excerpt: Accepted Change E deprecates FieldGroup as semantically subsumed but explicitly gates schema removal and instance migration on #242.
Merged PR #263 retained the deprecated members because the spec's own instance data still depended on them.

alternatives: Retain FieldGroup permanently as a parallel nesting mechanism.
Delete FieldGroup immediately before a conforming inline-composite carrier exists.
accepted_cost: A transitional duplicate surface remains visible and must be removed in a later all-or-nothing migration.
supersedes: FieldGroup as the preferred semantic nesting model

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Keeping two nesting semantics would preserve ambiguity; deleting the old carrier immediately would strand real values.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The transitional carrier preserves usable existing data until the semantic replacement is storable.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: The deprecated surface becomes a permanent second authority.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Either permanent legacy or immediate breakage would discard one of the explicitly protected concerns.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Evolution is ratified at the model layer while continuity is protected by a carrier prerequisite.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: The gate remains after its stated carrier precondition is satisfied.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Permanent parallel nesting mechanisms would encode the same meaning inconsistently.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The migration timing remains bounded by actual package data needs.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Consolidation erases a distinct local construct rather than a true duplicate.

coding_notes: The semantic replacement and carrier gate are coupled in the accepted migration disposition; continuity is deliberately balanced and excluded from bias counts.

title: Express the definition-layer metamodel in its own Field and Type language
decision_statement: Field, Type, FieldAssignment, and the in-scope value objects are authored as SRS definitions in the canonical com.semanticops.srs/metamodel package, replacing RFC-004's parallel schema-source vocabulary.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-033 defines the ten-Type self-hosted metamodel package and [R7] supersedes RFC-004's parallel vocabulary.
The current canonical metamodel package contains the generated Field and Type definitions.

alternatives: Keep RFC-004 schema-definition/schema-member as a second source language.
Define the metamodel only through hand-authored JSON Schema.
accepted_cost: The system must bootstrap a language expressed in itself and maintain closure evidence for a recursive package.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A parallel schema-source language would create two authorities for the same semantic definitions.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Generated JSON Schema remains the interoperable runtime expression.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Self-description is maintained ceremonially while runtime meaning diverges from it.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Retaining RFC-004's vocabulary would preserve historical work but perpetuate the duplicate source.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Its reusable projection rules are retained rather than discarded.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Consolidation deletes reusable historical contracts along with obsolete source artifacts.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Multiple schema vocabularies would let model meaning fork across toolchains.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Domain packages still author Types and Fields within the same shared language.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: The core metamodel claims concerns that belong to independent extension packages.

coding_notes: Scope is the definition layer; the RFC explicitly defers instance-layer Record/Relation/Container self-hosting.

title: Resolve the metamodel through ordinary packageRefs rather than implicit merge
decision_statement: The metamodel package is an explicit ordinary packageRef-resolved package; foundational status reserves its specific identities but does not make com.semanticops.srs implicitly available or reserve the entire namespace.

sources.excerpt: RFC-033 Rev 2 rejects its earlier always-implicit proposal, preserving RFC-029 packageRef resolution and reserving only specific metamodel identities.
The effective repository manifest resolves the metamodel by packageRef.

alternatives: Implicitly merge every com.semanticops.srs metamodel type into all repositories.
Reserve the entire namespace against package ownership.
accepted_cost: Repositories and tools that need metamodel records must resolve an explicit dependency even though the runtime seed is foundational.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Implicit availability would blur the distinct roles of runtime bootstrap schema and toolchain-consumed metamodel records.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The frozen seed is still always available to load records.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Layer purity forces users to configure dependencies that have no meaningful choice.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Implicit merge would break the existing package resolution contract established by RFC-029.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: A new metamodel package is still added through the established extension mechanism.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Legacy resolution rules block a demonstrably simpler bootstrap design.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: A namespace-wide implicit package would impose a hidden global dependency and reservation on every repository.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Specific canonical metamodel IDs and shared package resolution rules preserve coherence.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Explicit ownership permits repositories to substitute incompatible foundational definitions.

coding_notes: Preserves the original decision and explicit supersession of RFC-033 Rev 1 rather than rewriting the history.

title: Retain committed Field and Type schemas as the runtime bootstrap fixed point
decision_statement: The loader consumes committed field.json and type.json as-is and never derives them from the metamodel records at runtime, even after records become the build-time authorship source.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-033 [R3] makes the two schemas the bootstrap fixed point and forbids runtime re-derivation.
The effective schema is marked as the frozen seed loaded as committed.

alternatives: Re-derive the schema at process startup from records that themselves require the schema to parse.
Avoid self-hosted records and retain hand-authored schemas as the only representation.
accepted_cost: The project retains a bootstrap artifact in addition to the self-hosted records and must check them for drift at build time.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Runtime generation would require trusting records before their defining schema is available.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Self-hosted records remain inspectable and become the planned build-time authorship source.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: The bootstrap artifact becomes a second hand-edited semantic authority.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Removing the independent base case would make existing loaders unable to parse the definition of their own model.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The later authorship flip can regenerate the committed fixed point once closure is proven.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Bootstrap caution blocks the build-time source flip after all preconditions pass.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Implementations could invent different bootstrap derivations.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The fixed artifact is portable and does not require a particular generator at runtime.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: One committed artifact prevents independently conforming implementations.

coding_notes: Matches calibrated precedent E256-A91. The later authorship direction is not equivalent to runtime derivation.

title: Make projection loss explicit in a per-emitter fidelity contract
decision_statement: Every metamodel feature is classified as authoritative or approximated for each emitter; authoritative meaning cannot be silently dropped and approximated meaning must emit its documented lossy shape.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-033 [R5] requires a per-emitter authoritative/approximated classification and forbids silent omission.
The current dashboard records fidelity and coverage separately for the JSON Schema emitter.

alternatives: Describe generation as lossless despite known semantic gaps.
Silently omit constructs that a target cannot represent.
accepted_cost: Each emitter maintains an explicit feature matrix, lossy-shape contract, and tests rather than claiming simple universal equivalence.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A convenient target projection could silently erase semantics while still appearing valid.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Approximated output remains usable and is emitted in a documented form rather than prohibited.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Fidelity bookkeeping grows while no consumer depends on the distinctions.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Pretending complete fidelity would make adding new targets or improving approximations unsafe.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Existing approximated forms are named and can be preserved deliberately.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Fidelity categories change without migration consequences for existing consumers.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Each emitter could choose undisclosed losses and produce artifacts with incomparable meaning.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Targets may use different approximations as long as each is explicit and tested.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A common matrix prevents target-native representations that preserve more meaning.

coding_notes: Fidelity and metamodel coverage are explicitly separate; this card concerns fidelity only.

title: Gate data-model compatibility with a monotonic revision stamp
decision_statement: Manifests and generated bundles carry a monotonic non-negative dataModelRevision, with absence treated as revision 0 and the valueType-to-fieldType migration registered and stamped as revision 1.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-033 [R6] defines the integer generation stamp, absent-as-zero behavior, migration 1, and bundle propagation.
The effective repository manifest is stamped dataModelRevision 1.

alternatives: Use a 2.0.x semver-looking model version.
Use shape detection alone without a coarse compatibility gate.
Reject unstamped revision-0 repositories.
accepted_cost: The project maintains a separate coarse generation counter alongside artifact versions and must propagate it through migrations and bundles.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A semver-looking patch could falsely imply backward compatibility for a breaking data-model shape.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The integer is deliberately coarse; shape detection remains the precise mechanism.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: The stamp is mistaken for complete semantic compatibility proof.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Strictly requiring the new stamp would make legacy repositories unable to reach the migration; no gate would make newer repositories unsafe to load.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Absent means 0 for reachability, while newer-than-binary revisions fail closed.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Legacy defaulting conceals a repository whose actual shape disagrees with revision 0.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Repositories, generated bundles, and runtimes could disagree about the data-model generation.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The gate makes no claim about package versioning or domain-owned evolution.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A global revision blocks independently compatible package changes.

coding_notes: Balanced continuity/evolution is intentional and therefore off-cube for that axis.

title: Put a deterministic target-neutral IR between records and emitters
decision_statement: Projection resolves semantic meaning into a target-neutral IR, then deterministic target back ends render it; the JSON Schema back end reuses the shared per-field projection rather than defining another semantic mapping.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-035 [R1], [R6], and [R7] require a target-neutral semantic front half, deterministic output, and target-only back ends.
The merged reference implementation builds the neutral schema model and emits deterministic JSON Schema.

alternatives: Walk each Type and emit JSON Schema directly with no neutral seam.
Let every target independently interpret Field records.
accepted_cost: A stable IR and ordering contract are implemented before a second target exists.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Direct target emitters could let syntax silently choose semantic meaning.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Back ends retain freedom over target syntax after the semantic boundary.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: The neutral IR accumulates target-specific details or omits target-expressible meaning.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: A JSON-specific front half would require disruptive redesign when a second target arrives.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The JSON emitter reuses the proven projectField mapping and freezes deterministic goldens.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Speculative future targets overcomplicate the first emitter.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Each language could develop a separate interpretation of Field semantics.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Independent back ends can be added without changing the shared front half.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Shared IR rules prevent a target from expressing legitimate native capabilities.

coding_notes: Matches calibrated precedent E256-A92; deterministic ordering is part of the emitter seam's cross-implementation contract.

title: Replace impossible seed byte-equality with two strict, honest verification tiers
decision_statement: Emitter determinism is checked byte-for-byte against its own goldens, while semantic closure against the hand-authored seed is an explicit normalized emitter-subset relation with exclusions and registered divergences.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-035 refines RFC-033 R4(b): byte parity is against emitter goldens and seed closure uses reference resolution, explicit exclusions, and a divergence register.
The delivered closure test enforces the authoritative subset and reports exclusions and divergence.

alternatives: Require literal equality with a seed whose intentional structure cannot be regenerated.
Loosen or doctor the emitter and seed until a single superficial diff passes.
Use only a deterministic golden without semantic closure.
accepted_cost: Verification has two distinct gates plus an exclusion and divergence register that reviewers must maintain.
supersedes: RFC-033 R4(b) literal byte-for-byte seed wording

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A cosmetically simple equality claim would be false or would force semantic and structural distortions.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Byte-for-byte reproducibility remains strict where it is meaningful, against emitter-owned goldens.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Normalization and exclusions become loopholes that hide real drift.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserving accepted wording literally would make a correct emitter impossible to certify.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The earlier intent is explicitly preserved and the supersession is documented rather than silently rewritten.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Accepted obligations are weakened whenever implementation becomes inconvenient.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Different implementations could claim closure using undocumented normalizations.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Emitter-owned keys and target syntax remain locally selectable within the published comparison contract.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: One verification normalization masks target-specific correctness failures.

coding_notes: Original RFC-033 wording and RFC-035 supersession are both preserved in sources.

title: Bind Rust projection to the accepted fieldType and emitter contracts
decision_statement: The Rust implementation adopts the RFC-032 fieldType model and implements the RFC-035 projection through core, CLI, and WASM surfaces with byte-parity against the reference emitter rather than maintaining its earlier independent mapping.

sources.excerpt: Merged PR #778 reports fieldType adoption, reference-emitter byte parity for entity schemas and bundle, and CLI/WASM bindings.
RFC-035 makes the Rust service a binding of the sanctioned emitter rather than an independent projection.

alternatives: Keep the pre-RFC-032 Rust mapping as an independent source of projection semantics.
Leave the accepted model Node-only.
accepted_cost: Rust consumers underwent a breaking model migration and serialization ordering became part of cross-language parity.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: An independent mapping could produce usable schemas with meaning that diverged from the accepted projection.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The implementation exposes practical CLI and WASM surfaces and reports inexpressible constraints.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Byte parity is treated as sufficient even when two implementations share the same semantic defect.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Retaining the embedded legacy model would keep existing code stable but leave the binary unable to load the epic's records.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Revision-0 repositories load and can migrate; regression tests cover earlier behavior.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Implementation migration breaks consumers beyond the accepted model boundary.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Rust could become a second standards authority with its own mapping.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Rust chooses internal types and serialization machinery while matching the public contract.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Reference parity prevents a conforming implementation from choosing a better internal design.

coding_notes: Documented as a delivered consequence, not an additional bias vote; PR #778 also contains independent unknown-field and aiGuidance decisions assigned to other research families.

title: Keep cardinality on Field and repair migrated definitions rather than add assignment overrides
decision_statement: List cardinality remains semantic content of Field.fieldType; the two mistranslated table Fields are corrected to list and a corpus guard rejects deprecated assignment cardinality that disagrees, while requiredness remains Type-contextual.

sources.excerpt: The owner delivery record resolves the contradiction toward Field-level-only cardinality under Invariant 2 and preserves requiredness as contextual.
RFC-032 Revision 6 records the data repair and removes the contradictory assignment-override claim.
The merged guard catches the exact two pre-fix violations and enforces the corrected invariant.

alternatives: Add a new assignment-level cardinality override.
Trust deprecated repeatable until it disappears.
Move group occurrence bounds onto the nested cells Field.
accepted_cost: A Field cannot vary list cardinality by Type context; differing contextual shapes require distinct Fields, while a repository-wide guard adds validation work.
supersedes: Single-valued columns and cells migration result

integrity_expression.counterfactual: An assignment override would let a Type redefine semantic content owned by its Field, and leaving the mismatch would make arrays appear single-valued.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Requiredness remains contextual, and new Fields can model genuinely different cardinality.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Field identity proliferates solely to accommodate harmless contextual presentation needs.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Keeping the migrated definitions unchanged would preserve files but leave deprecated carrier state load-bearing and make later removal unsafe.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The repair changes only two Fields and preserves all record payloads; legacy trees are reported without being failed.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: A global invariant rewrites released legacy artifacts outside the active model.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Per-assignment cardinality would permit the same Field identity to mean single and list in different Types.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Type context continues to own workflow requiredness, and legacy package trees remain bounded exceptions.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Shared Field semantics prevent a Type from expressing a legitimate contextual constraint.

coding_notes: The correction is reasoned application because Invariant 2 decides between the two offered repairs. The later correction to an overstated render claim does not supersede this decision.

title: Move the cheaper generated package identity and enforce repository-wide uniqueness
decision_statement: The colliding generated metamodel package moves to the first never-claimed package UUID while the established hand-authored package retains its identity, and validation rejects duplicate resolved IDs or reuse of one package ID for different meanings across repository trees.

sources.excerpt: The owner acceptance requires reassignment of the generated package, regeneration, reference proof, and a uniqueness assertion as one repair.
Merged PR #299 selects never-claimed 4a000004, preserves established IDs, and documents negative validation.
The effective metamodel package carries the corrected 4a000004 identity.

alternatives: Move the older hand-authored package and its dependent definitions.
Recycle a previously claimed but inactive UUID.
Repair only the active collision without a cross-tree guard.
accepted_cost: The generated package identity changes and validation scans active, released, fixture, and proposal trees to prevent resolution-order ambiguity from recurring.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Leaving or narrowly hiding the collision would make two semantic packages one resolution key.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The cheaper generated side moves, avoiding a broad hand-authored migration.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Identity repair triggers rewrites beyond the smallest conflicting boundary.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserving the newer generated ID would require accepting the collision or moving the older, more connected package.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: All definition UUIDs, the established package, and claimed-ID history remain stable; claimed IDs are not recycled.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Corrective reassignment breaks external consumers after an identity has escaped the repository.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Checking only one active tree would allow package identity to mean different things in distribution, fixture, or proposal contexts.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Copies and revisions may repeat an ID when namespace/name meaning is the same; cross-kind reuse only warns.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Repository-wide checks prohibit legitimate copies or version variation of the same identified package.

coding_notes: Matches calibrated precedent E256-A93. The reassignment and guard stay together because the owner explicitly made prevention part of the repair acceptance.
